question.text: A ball of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is attached to a string of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The ball is rotated on a horizontal circular path about its vertical axis. The maximum tension that the string can bear is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>400</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>. The maximum possible value of angular velocity of the ball in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is,:

solution.text:
Let the string makes angle θ with the vertical. Weight will be balanced by the vertical component of tension, which is Tcosθ=mg and the horizontal component towards the centre will provide the required centripetal force for circular motion. Therefore,

Tsinθ=mω2lsinθ, where l=length of the string.

⇒400sinθ=0.5ω2×0.5sinθ

⇒ω=40 rad s-1
